programmes.d: Responding to a 2008 garage fire, Illinois emergency response discovered a man crushed beneath a truck.
Lack of evidence compels investigators to look beyond the obvious when a woman is beaten to death.
When a hit-and-run boating accident caused the death of a popular young man, investigators faced the daunting task of searching for one boat among 1200 others.
A photographer claims model Linda Sobek died during a consensual sexual encounter gone wrong.
How did the stalker obtain the security system code for his victim's home? How did he steal her personal photographs? Police needed answers and they found them in the most unlikely of places.
A woman's deadly walk in the woods was ruled a hunting accident until a strange letter appeared.

Survivors of Nazi atrocities recognized Archbishop Trifa, former head of the Romanian Orthodox Church in America, as having directed a bloody attack against Jews during World War II. He was deported in 1984 and died three years later.
There was no clear reason for a young, healthy college student to be dead.

Residents of Noel, Missouri were stunned to learn that their bank had been robbed and the bank president was missing. His body was later found floating in a lake, securely bound to a chair with duct tape.
A flight attendant's brutal murder prompts the son of another victim to contact the police.

The murder of an American tourist in a Mexican resort draws law enforcement resources on both sides of the border. At first glance, the motive appears to be robbery, but careful analysis of the forensic evidence points to something more sinister.
More than 700 Oregonians contracted food poisoning from a unique strain of salmonella in 1984.
In a quiet village in Great Britain, a farmer came upon a chilling sight.

There was no clear reason for a young, healthy college student to be dead. But when the coroner discovered a tiny clue during the autopsy, investigators were able to uncover a mystery filled with betrayal and revenge.
A man has no recollection of events after stabbing his wife and drowning her in the pool.
It was a tragic twist of fate. Just days after a woman sold her home and moved to a modest trailer, a fire took both the trailer and her life. But the autopsy proved this was no accident.
In 1984 police failed to convict the murderer of a college student.

Avis Banks and her unborn child were brutally murdered. The body was discovered by her fiancé, Keyon Pittman. When police learned that Pittman was having affairs with other women, he became the prime suspect.
When a successful stockbroker doesn't return home after a late shift, his wife reports him missing.

In 2007, the Florida mobile home of Effie and Michael Ratley catches fire. Michael heroically rescues his wife and infant son. A month later, his wife is found beaten to death in a bedroom of his parents' home.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.

A two-man shrimp boat sinks when a fast-moving, violent storm strikes the Louisiana coast. The captain drowns, but the deckhand is rescued fourteen hours later. The crewman is hailed as a hero — until the captain's body is discovered.
A suspect is profiled in the disappearance of a 6-year-old girl during a church service.

While vacationing in California, Earl Morris learns that his wife has gone missing from their Arizona home. The search for Ruby Morris involves dozens of investigators and scientists — and even the Coast Guard.
A police investigation uncovers a web of homeless drifters, cattle auctions and bad checks.

It was one of the most unusual cases in forensic history. Investigators had to find a way to solve a murder case using only a squashed tomato found at the crime scene and tiny, pinpoint reflections of light in a photograph.
In 1986, Gary Dale Larson was stabbed to death in his Edmond, Oklahoma home.
When a talented television news anchor is shot to death outside her home, it appears to be a crime of passion perpetrated by an obsessed fan.
A bullet-riddled car, a missing driver, and no witnesses. Was this an ambush or a random attack?

A woman was brutally murdered in her home and the only witnesses to the crime were the family dogs. An expert in canine behavior was convinced the killer knew both the victim and the animals, and he was determined find out what the dogs had seen.
An assistant manager of a Florida steakhouse is stabbed to death.

When convenience store employee Wanda Mason is found dead, investigators find the entire murder has been caught on the store's security camera. But the image of the killer is so degraded it seems impossible to positively identify him.
When a dedicated teacher disappeared, police had to determine if she was the victim of foul play.
A family vacation turns into a nightmare when a woman is found face-down in a lake.
A woman is killed weeks before testifying against the man who sexually assaulted her.

In 1996, police received a call from Darlie Routier telling them of her two sons' murders. The police found the killer by analyzing blood spatter, doing behavioral profiling and analyzing Darlie's 911 call.
For seven years, a trio of men robbed one bank after another.
The victim was a self-made man who never minced words. Perhaps he was murdered by a disgruntled client or employee. Perhaps the racy photos in his safe held the clue to solving the crime.
In 2000, Kristine Fitzhugh failed to show up for her music class and her husband Ken found her dead.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause millions of dollars worth of damage and the deaths of three people. He is discovered, partly through the use of forensic hypnosis.
In 1993, the Amtrak Railroad experienced the deadliest train crash in United States history.

Casino security cameras tracked a young woman's movements until shortly before she disappeared. She was never seen again, but through the evidence she left behind, she was able to tell investigators what happened to her and who was responsible.
A woman appears to have plunged her car into a creek. But investigators suspect foul play.
Faced with three homicides that appear to be professional executions, investigators on both sides of the Atlantic must find a common thread between the victims.
Police investigate the shooting of a homicide detective's wife.

Investigators are baffled after finding a murder scene devoid of any physical evidence, but they suspect that the victim's dog had witnessed the crime. If so, forensic scientists would have to find some way to learn what the dog had seen.
After shooting his victims, the killer placed the evidence into a bag and tossed it into the river.

Women in a Louisiana city live in fear of a rapist who leaves no clues to his identity. But technology and behavioral science combine to give police a new forensic tool. Police narrow their search to one man: local policeman Randy Comeaux.
Serial arsonist leaves no evidence.
When a nine-year-old girl goes missing, police and volunteers spend weeks searching for her.

Firefighters find an entire family dead inside their home in an apparent murder-suicide, but there are several inconsistent clues in the rubble. Could ballistics, a time card and some secret audiotapes unravel the mystery?
When hunters found a skull in a Texas canyon, a forensic artist was able to reconstruct her face.
In 2004, Mary Ann Clibbery was found brutally murdered at her Illinois business. Investigators had to determine if this was a robbery gone wrong or a calculated murder.
In 2002, funeral director Lonnie Turner, Sr. was found shot to death.
Authorities track a kidnapper who let his victim write a last will and informed the family of her murder. A phone number written on a previous page left a lasting impression, which helped to convict.
A college student was found dead, and the evidence suggested he knew his killer.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
In 1991, Maine resident Pearl Smith is missing after an argument with her husband Bill Bruns.

Just weeks before a witness is to testify against the man accused of sexually assaulting her, she is murdered in the front yard of her own home. Investigators immediately suspect her attacker, but they don't have enough evidence to prove his guilt.

One investigator's quick thinking helps him capture a shoe impression made in snow before the evidence melts away. The shoe leads investigators to Peter Benedict and Frank Lanoue, who are convicted of aggravated assault and robbery.
With the use of DNA profiling, an innocent man is freed and the real killer is convicted.
After 6-year-old Michelle Lee Dorr went missing, her father confessed to murdering her.
In 2000, teenager Tara Munsey went missing after a work shift at a Virginia restaurant. Did she run away, or was she the victim of foul play?
A young girl beaten after watching her grandmother killed, identifies the wrong person.
Mark Fair left for work and his fiancée, Karla Brown, stayed home. Later, he found her dead. During the autopsy, bite marks on her body were re-examined and forensic odontology identified the killer.
A young bride-to-be is gunned down and investigators uncover the man she loved was living a lie.

Between 1985 and 1988, 18 people were choked, molested and left for dead in the remote mountains of California. The only witnesses were the insects — and they play an important role in solving the crimes and bringing the killer to justice.
An obscure style of rope and forensic analysis lead to the arrest and conviction of a murderer.
On October 15, 1985, two bomb explosions rocked Salt Lake City and resulted in two deaths. A third explosion occurred the next day; this time, the victim survived.
When a heart surgeon is found dead, investigators uncover his new wife's history of violence.

When a popular gym teacher is found dead of what appears to be an accidental gunshot wound, his family is suspicious. A tape recorded by the victim just before his death tells the true story of his strange marriage and his wife's insatiable greed.
A woman was killed instantly when a bomb exploded in her home. Who planted the bomb?

Susie Mowbray was charged in her husband's death. Her son was so convinced of her innocence that he enrolled in law school, studied all of the evidence and, eventually, discovered the truth of what really happened between his parents.
In the 1980s, a trio of unsolved murders occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas.

A woman disappears and her husband becomes the prime suspect — especially after police find a huge bloodstain on the carpet of their bedroom. When they spray the bedroom with Luminol, they discover it was awash with blood spatter.
A woman and her soon-to-be ex-husband are murdered shortly after she meets a man online.

The woman had been sexually assaulted, stabbed repeatedly and left for dead. When a perfect suspect practically turned himself in, police were sure they had their man — until DNA evidence proved them wrong.
In 1986, scientists and detectives use DNA to solve a string of rapes and murders in the UK.

A human skeleton was discovered in the North Carolina marshlands. When investigators learned she'd been dead for 18 months, they knew it would be difficult to find out who she was, let alone who killed her.
Police collect evidence leading to a driver who fatally injured a cyclist in a hit-and-run accident.

A brilliant young architect falls ill and dies just before she is to testify in a criminal trial. The autopsy reveals she'd been poisoned with arsenic. Investigators must determine who had a motive for murder.
A woman disappeared and her husband became the prime suspect.
When police recovered the submerged car of a missing man, they expected to find his body — but it wasn't there. The investigation that followed would uncover an obsession turned deadly.
The body of a Connecticut man is found in a burning rental car in Mexico.
A Colorado hunter is the victim of a well-planned crime. Investigators suspect two weapons and two killers. But forensic evidence points them in a different direction — one much closer to home.
A mother of two vanishes after a shopping trip. Her body is discovered a month later.
In 1995, when off-duty Maine State Trooper Vicky Gardner is attacked by Steven Fortin during a routine stop, it triggers a chain of events which jumpstart a stalled murder case in New Jersey.
The prime suspect's driver's license was found at the scene of a brutal double homicide.

It was supposed to be a routine motorcade for the Queen of England. But on the way to Yosemite National Park, a car carrying three Secret Service agents collided with a car driven by a deputy from the local sheriff's office.
When a woman went missing, friends and family were determined to find her.

Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a crime scene where one man had been killed and two teenage girls were seriously injured. Neither of the girls could identify their attacker, but one simple clue helped track the footsteps of a killer.
When a hit-and-run accident killed a high school athlete, everyone in town searched for the killer.

When four-month-old Ryan Stallings dies under suspicious circumstances, his mother is ultimately convicted of his murder. But months later, new evidence emerges from a startling source — his newborn brother.
Lives changed in the 20 years following an unsolved murder, and so did forensic science.
In 1999, 9-year-old Valiree Jackson vanished on her way to school near Spokane. Her father, Brad Jackson, reported the disappearance and the entire community started searching for her abductor.
An infant was rushed to the emergency room with serious breathing problems.

When the decomposed body of a teenage girl is discovered, police have no clues to her identity. To solve the case, investigators turn to bug larvae found on the body and a tiny wad of chewing gum found near the victim's body.
A dismembered body is dumped on the side of the New Jersey Turnpike.
In 1991, Dorothy Donovan was murdered in her Dover, Delaware home.
